newsitem.title: ITALY: Italians rescue foreigners from Albanian port.
newsitem.headline: Italians rescue foreigners from Albanian port.

text.p: Terrified Albanians, fearing an imminent military crackdown, begged foreign reporters not to leave the southern port of Vlore on Monday as gunmen fired wildly from speeding cars.
As a group of reporters and Italian citizens waited at a rundown airstrip outside the southern port for Italian military helicopters, locals appealed to them to stay.
"If you leave we'll be alone. Whose going to report what's going on here?" they said.
The foreigners flew out after Albania's government declared a state of emergency on Sunday, giving the security forces power to open fire to disperse crowds.
The government also warned armed insurgents in the south of the country that they would be shot without warning unless they surrendered their weapons by 1300 GMT on Monday.
While reporters waited at the old military airport, not knowing when the Italian helicopters would arrive, a hand grenade exploded on the tarmac.

Conditions in the Adriatic port had become increasingly chaotic with armed rioters putting police and soldiers to flight. The airstrip had no perimeter fence and gunmen raced in and out, occasionally firing their weapons.

Vlore was the scene on Friday night of the worst violence in two months of unrest in Albania, Europe's poorest state, following the collapse of pyramid savings schemes which had soaked up many people's life savings.
Up to nine people, three of them civilians, were reported killed in the Friday gun battle between demonstrators and Shik secret policemen.
When the helicopters came into view, two small Scout attack ones from a nearby Italian navy frigate flanking two huge Chinook transports, it was like something out of the movies.
The whole operation on the ground lasted about eight minutes, from the moment the armed Italian marines leaped to the tarmac in combat positions to the final take off.

The waiting press and Italians ran to the helicopters, leaped in and the marines gave the all clear to leave. No shots were fired by or at the Italians and there was no sign of the gunmen who had made their presence felt before.

The Italian foreign ministry said 35 people had been evacuated, including 20 Italians, four Germans, a Dutch citizen and 10 reporters from various other countries including at least three Greek nationals.
All were flown to the southern Italian port of Brindisi.
The ministry said the situation in Tirana, the surrounding areas and the port of Durres was calm.

"At the moment no further evacuation operations of Italian citizens in Albania are planned," the ministry said in a statement. However it repeated a call for Italians to go to Albania only in cases of absolute necessity.
"In any case, it is absolutely not advised to go to Vlora or the southern parts of the country," it said.
